chunks: From him, from al-Abbas, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who marries off his female slave to his male slave: does she stand to him [in terms of marital rights/privacy] as she used to stand to him, so he sees her uncovered or sees her in that state? He disliked that and said, 'My father prevented me from marrying off some of my servants, my male slave, for that reason.'

key_terms.تَقُومُ عَلَيْهِ: she stands to him / her status towards him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a female slave to a male slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the legal bond of marriage between a female slave and her master's male slave remains valid, he disliked the arrangement due to the potential loss of modesty (haya) when the master might see her uncovered. This ruling reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential concern for maintaining the dignity and privacy of slaves within the household, a precedent established by his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS), who explicitly prohibited such unions to preserve these ethical standards.
